      coderabbitai[bot] commented on May 8, 2026

      coderabbitai[bot]
      on May 8, 2026
      More actions

      ⚠️ Potential issue | 🟠 Major | ⚡ Quick win

      Subsection modes conflate permission capability with edit session state.

      These variables (carTestsMode, securityTestsMode, counterReadingsMode) represent whether the user can edit, not whether they are currently editing. Using them directly as subsection mode causes:

      • Users with UPDATE permission see subsections in EDIT mode on page load
      • Clicking "Cancel" on the parent section sets existingToolSectionModes.expiredTests to VIEW, but subsections remain editable
      • Header shows "View" while content remains editable

      The readPermission/updatePermission props (correctly set on the subsections) already gate the Edit button via form-section-header.tsx. Subsection mode should follow the parent section mode.

      🔧 Suggested fix

      Remove these permission-based mode variables entirely, or rename them to clarify they're capabilities (e.g., canEditCarTests) if needed elsewhere. Subsection mode should use the parent:

      -  const carTestsMode = hasPermission(
-    permissions,
-    toolPermissions.CAR_TESTS.UPDATE,
-  )
-    ? EMode.EDIT
-    : EMode.VIEW;
-  const securityTestsMode = hasPermission(
-    permissions,
-    toolPermissions.SECURITY_TESTS.UPDATE,
-  )
-    ? EMode.EDIT
-    : EMode.VIEW;
-  const counterReadingsMode = hasPermission(
-    permissions,
-    toolPermissions.COUNTER_READINGS.UPDATE,
-  )
-    ? EMode.EDIT
-    : EMode.VIEW;

      Then update all subsection mode usages (lines 216, 239, 380, 527, 547, 717, 890, 900, 1015) to:

      mode: existingToolSectionModes.expiredTests ?? EMode.VIEW,

      As per coding guidelines: "Gate detail-page Edit / Save / Cancel by setting readPermission and updatePermission on every FormSectionConfig... form-section-header.tsx enforces this automatically."

      Subsection modes should derive from section state, not permissions.

      Per coding guidelines, mode should reflect actual section state; permissions should only gate the Edit button via updatePermission.

      ⚠️ Potential issue | 🔴 Critical | ⚡ Quick win

      Subsection modes should derive from parent section state, not permissions alone.

      The mode variables (carTestsMode, securityTestsMode, counterReadingsMode) are computed solely from UPDATE permissions. This causes subsections to render in EDIT mode on page load for any user with update capability—even while existingToolSectionModes.expiredTests is still VIEW. Clicking Cancel resets the parent to VIEW, but these permission-derived modes remain EDIT, leaving subsections editable while headers show "View."

      Per coding guidelines, readPermission and updatePermission on FormSectionConfig gate the Edit/Save/Cancel buttons; the mode prop should track actual UI state.

      More actions

      ⚠️ Potential issue | 🔴 Critical | ⚡ Quick win

      Subsection modes are derived purely from permissions, ignoring parent section state.

      These mode variables are computed solely from hasPermission(...UPDATE), making them static throughout the component lifecycle. They don't track existingToolSectionModes.expiredTests, so:

      1. Users with UPDATE permission see subsections in EDIT mode on page load before clicking Edit.
      2. Clicking Cancel resets the parent to VIEW but subsections remain editable (these modes don't change).
